stimulus.text: Paraphrase: In June 1941, President Franklin D. Roosevelt issued Executive Order 8802. The order banned discrimination in defense industries and in government training programs because of race, creed, color, or national origin. It also created the Fair Employment Practices Committee to receive and investigate complaints. The order came after the labor leader A. Philip Randolph, head of the Brotherhood of Sleeping Car Porters, threatened a large march on Washington to protest discrimination in war jobs.
stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of Executive Order 8802, June 25, 1941. Randolph's threatened March on Washington, planned for July 1941, was called off after the order.

source: original; stimulus paraphrased from Executive Order 8802 (June 25, 1941)
stem: Randolph's threatened march led to the order. This sequence best shows which of the following?

options.text: The president acted only after Congress passed a new law
options.misconception: No law was passed; Roosevelt acted by executive order.

options.text: Organized protest could move the federal government to act on civil rights
The Supreme Court ordered the president to end discrimination
options.misconception: The Court played no part in Executive Order 8802.

options.text: Labor unions opposed any role for Black workers in war plants
options.misconception: Randolph was a labor leader pressing for Black workers to get war jobs.

rationales.A: Roosevelt issued the order himself; Congress passed no law behind it.
rationales.B: A planned mass march, backed by an organized union, pressed Roosevelt to act before the march took place.
rationales.C: The order came from the president, not from a court ruling.
rationales.D: Randolph led a Black labor union, and his march aimed to open war jobs to Black workers.
rationales.general:
1. War plants were turning Black workers away, and Randolph planned a march to protest it.
2. Roosevelt heard of the plan and negotiated instead of letting the march happen.
3. The result was an executive order banning discrimination in defense work.
4. The protest did not win everything, but it moved the president to act.
Remember: pressure that is organized and public can move a president even without a new law.
